_comment: Structures across verses and chapters, shown from Deep behind the commentary notice: bookends (inclusio), refrains, two threads taking turns (alternation), mirrors (chiasm) and foils (two people set side by side, whose sides may hold several ranges across chapters and books). Checked by crates/atlas-cli/src/extra_structure.rs.

members are the passage's parts in reading order, each with its mark (A and A' for bookends, R for a refrain, A B A B for turns, A B B' A' for a mirror) and its exact BSB words from one verse of its ref; tie, on the first member of each group that answers one another, is words found in every member of the group.

cites follow config/figure-forms.json: only its quotable works are quoted, the cite list in config/layer-sources.json says who wrote each book's words, and strength is the number of different interpreters cited (3 or more widely agreed, 2 commonly held, 1 some interpreters). docs/evidence/structures-2026-11-01.json records where each quote was read.

kinds.label: Bookends
kinds.about: A passage opens and closes with the same words, so the end takes the reader back to the start.

kinds.label: A refrain
kinds.about: The same words come back at set places, like the chorus of a song.

kinds.label: Taking turns
kinds.about: The account moves back and forth between two threads, so each shows up the other.

kinds.label: A mirror
kinds.about: The parts come in one order and then in reverse, A B then B A, often with the turn at the centre.

kinds.label: Set side by side
kinds.about: Two people, often chapters or books apart, are set side by side, and each shows up the other.

structures.short: Psalm 8 opens and closes with the same words

structures.short: One refrain runs through Psalms 42 and 43
structures.about: Three times the psalmist asks his soul why it is downcast and tells it to hope in God, twice in Psalm 42 and once more at the end of Psalm 43.

structures.evidence: Barnes: the same burden or refrain marks the parts, at 42:5, 42:11 and 43:5. Henry: the fifth verse of Psalm 43 is the same as the eleventh of Psalm 42. Fausset notes the recurrence of the refrain. Bullinger: a three-fold emphasis.
structures.limit: Writers differ on whether Psalms 42 and 43 were first written as one psalm; the refrain is in both either way.

cites.quote: Psa 42:1-11 consists of two parts, marked by the "burden" or "refrain" in Psa 42:5, Psa 42:11; and if Psa 43:1-5 were regarded as a part of the same composition, the two would be divided into three parts, marked by the same burden or refrain, in Psa 42:5, Psa 42:11; Psa 43:5.
